{"sha":"bcbec0eabcfa79d99921d04583afcbf9132906d7","node_id":"C_kwDOVuMIIdoAKGJjYmVjMGVhYmNmYTc5ZDk5OTIxZDA0NTgzYWZjYmY5MTMyOTA2ZDc","commit":{"author":{"name":"Gabriel Borg","email":"gabriel_borg1@hotmail.com","date":"2026-11-17T11:46:59Z"},"committer":{"name":"Gabriel Borg","email":"gabriel_borg1@hotmail.com","date":"2026-11-17T11:46:59Z"},"message":"feat(annotator)!: work in progress lives in the annotator's Postgres, and Lance is written only at publish

The labels people make on the canvas are now kept in one place: the task's draft in the annotator's own Postgres. The
canvas reads an item's work from the draft (still as Arrow rows, built from the draft, with the draft's revision as
X-Annotations-Version) and each save sends only what changed (inserts, edits, geometry, times, spans, deletes and, when
they changed, the item's links), which the store applies to the draft in one transaction under the task's row lock. The
revision check is per task: a stale or missing revision is a 409 for that task alone, never because of a save elsewhere
in the project. Every rule the save enforced still holds on this path: the per-save bounds and validation of times,
offsets, ids, groups and shape types, the unit and task scoping (a task's work is its item's first unit), the replica
rule, only the claim's holder or a reviewer of work in review writes, and the ontology at submit. A shape drawn and then
changed before a save arrives as its insert and its change together, and both apply. A relation drawn on its own is now
saved (it used to be saved nowhere), a deleted shape's links go with it, and a link naming a shape the work lacks is
refused. The tag door writes its tag rows into the named task's draft, insert-if-absent by their deterministic id, with
the same per-task check.

A task's draft is held to caps whichever door changes it (the save, the tag batch, the import), checked in the store's
one transaction after the change applies and before anything is written: 10,000 shapes, 10,000 links and 8 MiB of the
draft serialized as JSON (Postgres stores jsonb in its own form, so the stored size is close to this, not equal),
each refused with a 413 that names the cap. Ten thousand boxes serialize to about 4.7 MB (measured 470 bytes
a box), so the byte cap leaves a densely boxed page room for its texts and holds drafts of fewer, larger shapes; larger
items are the one-row-per-shape addition, deferred until needed. A tag batch names at most as many rows as a save
(5,000 labels in all, each at most 128 characters). A change that changes nothing (an empty save, a re-tag) writes
nothing and answers the current revision, so it takes no history slot.

The history panel reads a bounded history in Postgres (draft_history): who saved each revision and when, how many
shapes it left, and what undoes it (the shapes as they were before it for every shape it changed or removed, the ids it
added, and the links before it when it changed them). A past save is rebuilt from the current draft by undoing the saves
after it, and reads back with ?version=. The history keeps a task's last 50 saves within 8 MiB, trimmed in the
transaction of the save that pushes one out. Storing each save's undo rather than a whole copy is what makes the bound
affordable: an autosave's undo is about a kilobyte, so fifty cost about 50 KB, and a task's worst case is about one
capped draft and a full history, 8 + 8 = 16 MiB (a little over, since the newest save's undo is always kept even when it
alone passes 8 MiB), where fifty whole copies of a capped draft would have been 400 MiB. A past save rebuilt this way
holds the same shapes and links as it did, compared by id and content; a shape a later save removed comes back at the
end rather than in its old place, and no reader depends on the order. The panel
says who made each save, and reads the history again after each save that lands (it used to keep naming its first
read's newest save "current").

Labeling no longer needs a lakehouse. A source marked annotatable is labelled with no rask source declared; only a
publish needs one, and with none the publish door refuses before the project moves: "this deployment reads no rask
lakehouse, so there is nowhere to publish to". The publish itself still writes the final table through the catalog's
doors as before.

Deleted, because only the per-project Lance working table needed it: annotations/store.py, commit.py and lineage.py
(the working table, its write ritual and its OpenLineage emission), client_kit.lancekit.openlineage and its two test
files and vendored schema (no other user), the catalog transport's merge and delete doors and the workbench's own
lakehouse client helpers (as_workbench, lakehouse_writer), the ANNOTATOR_ANNOTATIONS_NAMESPACE and
ANNOTATOR_LINEAGE_SINK settings, the chart's auth.annotationsNamespace and its env, the declaration rule and the chart
refusal that a marked source needs a lakehouse, scripts/seed_annotations.py, the app's draft-sync.ts and draft-shapes.ts
(the second write after every save), its separate read of the draft's links at open, and the whole-draft PUT door
/tasks/{id}/draft, whose only caller was that second write (imports still write the draft, through the same
transactional change). The lakehouse grants script and make dev-grants now grant the workbench's own identity only
reader on the warehouses it signs media links for (--reads acme): no annotations namespace is created and no writer is
granted.

Two defects from the cluster walk, in the canvas: the side panel's "Not submitted…" refusal stayed after a later save
landed (it is now shown only until the next save that lands), and an autosave that landed left an earlier "Save
failed…" notice and its paused autosave in place (a landed save now clears both).

A save into a project frozen with a publish is refused at the save door and writes nothing, as the whole-draft door's
test used to pin.

The temporal canvas called itself ready (data-ready, no aria-busy) while the page's view transition was still running,
and during a transition the browser hit-tests every press to the root element: a region dragged in that window landed
on <html>, made no region and opened no class picker (measured: the press point read <html> before the drag and the
strip's canvas after it). The canvas now counts a running transition as not ready, as the image and text canvases
already did. This was the flaky browser test of a dragged region, which failed on main too.

Owner decision "Update unstarted items" (2026-11-17), folded in: when a project's ontology changes, every task of it
nobody has started (unassigned, never held, no draft) takes the new ontology in the same transaction, under the
project's write lock; a task someone claimed, drew on or submitted keeps the one it captured. The send dialog's "Create
and send" now asks for the label classes and their shape kind, as the New project form does, and cannot create a
project with none.

union 7102 -> 7018 (the working table's store, commit ritual and lineage emitter, the OpenLineage builders, the merge
and delete doors and the whole-draft door are gone; the draft-backed doors and the history replace them)
tests: +21 -52 (python +20 -48: the working-table, lineage and whole-draft door tests moved onto the draft-backed doors, the tests of deleted code deleted, the caps, the byte-bounded history and the frozen-project save pinned; vitest -4: draft-shapes.test.ts; Playwright +1: the panel's refusal clears after a later save, and the auth, relation, mouse-box and create-and-send specs changed in place)

-def column_lineage_facet(producer: str, edges: Iterable[ColumnEdge]) -> dict[str, object]:
-    """The standard ``ColumnLineageDatasetFacet`` payload for an output dataset's field-to-field provenance.

-    ``edges`` is an iterable of :data:`ColumnEdge` tuples; they are grouped by ``out_field`` into the
-    spec's ``fields[out].inputFields[].transformations[]`` shape (``lineage.models.Dataset.column_edges``
-    parses exactly this back out). Returns ``{}`` when there are no well-formed edges — an empty facet must
-    not materialise junk ``(:Column {field:""})`` on the consumer. One builder so the ``_schemaURL``
-    version stays consistent across every emitter; a per-emitter copy would silently drift (#24).
-    """
-    grouped: dict[str, list[dict[str, object]]] = {}
-    for out_field, ns, name, in_field, ttype, subtype, masking in edges:
-        # Guard the three identity keys (symmetric with the consumer's name/field/out guards): a malformed
-        # edge with an empty output or source column must not create a junk vertex on ingest.
-        if not out_field or not name or not in_field:
-            continue

-            {

-                "field": str(in_field),

-            }
-        )
-    if not grouped:
-        return {}
-    fields = {out_field: {"inputFields": inputs} for out_field, inputs in grouped.items()}

-    ``required`` is decided by WHAT THE WRITE CAN DESTROY, not by uniformity (#50):
-
-    * The per-unit review save (``save.py``) commits a ``merge_upsert`` — matched rows are

-      required: an optional precondition is not a precondition, and while ``None`` was
-      accepted any caller could opt out of concurrency control by simply omitting the field.
-      Two people on one page, or one person in two tabs, then silently overwrite each other —
-      the exact outcome this check exists to prevent. A draft save answers the identical
-      question the same way (``annotator.state.store.AnnotatorStore.save_draft``).
-    * The tag batch (``tags.py``) commits ``merge_insert_only`` — matched rows are left AS-IS,
-      so an add cannot clobber anything by construction. Its OCC is also table-GLOBAL across a

+"""A task's work in progress as the canvas reads and changes it: its draft's shapes as rows, and a save applied to them.
+
+Pure: no store and no request. The doors (`annotator.annotations.wire`, `.save`, `.tags`) run these on the draft the
+store's transaction read (`annotator.state.store.AnnotatorStore.change_draft`), so a change is judged and written on
+rows that cannot move under it.
+
+A save names rows by id, and every id it edits, moves or deletes must be one of the task's draft: one that is not is
+refused with the ids it named (404), and nothing is written. A new shape takes an id of its own (409 when the draft
+holds it). The server stamps who wrote each touched row and when; the caller's claim to either is never read.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from datetime import datetime
+from typing import Final
+
+import pyarrow as pa
+
+from annotator.annotations.schema import EMPTY_SCHEMA, NewAnnotation, SaveAnnotations
+from annotator.annotations.unit import Unit
+from annotator.projects.models import Draft, Link, Shape
+from service_kit.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError, ValidationError
+
+
+#: How many ids a refusal names: enough to find them, bounded so a refusal is never as large as the save.
+NAMED_IDS: Final = 20
+
+
+def attributes_of(metadata: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """The ontology's attribute map a row's ``metadata`` JSON carries: an object, its values as strings (a number or a
+    boolean spelled as JSON is the same value), nested values as their JSON text.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValidationError: ``metadata`` is not a JSON object.
+    """
+    try:
+        parsed = json.loads(metadata) if metadata else {}
+    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
+        raise ValidationError(f"metadata is not valid JSON ({exc})") from exc
+    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
+        raise ValidationError("metadata is a JSON object of attributes")
+    return {str(k): v if isinstance(v, str) else ("" if v is None else json.dumps(v, separators=(",", ":"))) for k, v in parsed.items()}
+
+
+def _metadata(attributes: dict[str, str]) -> str:
+    return json.dumps(attributes, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True)
+
+
+def _new_shape(row: NewAnnotation, *, author: str, now: datetime) -> Shape:
+    return Shape(
+        shape_id=row.id,
+        shape_type=row.shape_type,
+        x=row.x,
+        y=row.y,
+        width=row.width,
+        height=row.height,
+        rotation=row.rotation,
+        polygon=list(row.polygon),
+        t_start=row.t_start,
+        t_end=row.t_end,
+        parent_id=row.parent_id or None,
+        char_start=row.char_start if row.char_start >= 0 else None,
+        char_end=row.char_end if row.char_end >= 0 else None,
+        mask=row.mask or None,
+        label=row.label,
+        text=row.text,
+        attributes=attributes_of(row.metadata),
+        group=row.group or None,
+        source=row.source,
+        confidence=row.confidence,
+        uncertainty=row.uncertainty,
+        status=row.status,
+        reviewer=author,
+        created_at=now,
+        updated_at=now,
+    )
+
+
+def _refuse_unheld(ids: set[str], held: dict[str, Shape]) -> None:
+    if unknown := sorted(ids - held.keys()):
+        raise NotFoundError(f"annotation(s) {unknown[:NAMED_IDS]} are not this task's rows of its unit")
+
+
+def apply_save(draft: Draft | None, body: SaveAnnotations, *, author: str, now: datetime) -> tuple[list[Shape], list[Link]]:
+    """The draft's shapes and links once ``body`` is applied to them.
+
+    Raises:
+        NotFoundError: The save edits, moves or deletes an id the draft does not hold.
+        ConflictError: A new shape names an id the draft holds.
+        ValidationError: A metadata edit is not a JSON object, or a link names a shape the draft will not hold.
+    """
+    shapes = {s.shape_id: s.model_copy() for s in (draft.shapes if draft else [])}
+    links = list(draft.links) if draft else []
+    if held := sorted({i.id for i in body.inserts} & shapes.keys()):
+        raise ConflictError(f"annotation(s) {held[:NAMED_IDS]} already exist: a new shape takes an id of its own")
+    # New shapes first: the canvas sends a shape drawn and then moved, relabelled or deleted before the save as its
+    # insert and those changes together, by its new id.
+    for row in body.inserts:
+        shapes[row.id] = _new_shape(row, author=author, now=now)
+    named = {e.id for e in body.edits} | {g.id for g in body.geometry} | {t.id for t in body.temporal} | {s.id for s in body.spans} | set(body.deletes)
+    _refuse_unheld(named, shapes)
+
+    touched: set[str] = set()
+    for edit in body.edits:
+        shape = shapes[edit.id]
+        for field in ("label", "status", "text", "group"):
+            value = getattr(edit, field)
+            if value is not None:
+                setattr(shape, field, value)
+        if edit.metadata is not None:
+            shape.attributes = attributes_of(edit.metadata)
+        touched.add(edit.id)
+    for move in body.geometry:
+        shape = shapes[move.id]
+        shape.x, shape.y, shape.width, shape.height, shape.polygon = move.x, move.y, move.width, move.height, list(move.polygon)
+        touched.add(move.id)
+    for stretch in body.temporal:
+        shapes[stretch.id].t_start, shapes[stretch.id].t_end = stretch.t_start, stretch.t_end
+        touched.add(stretch.id)
+    for span in body.spans:
+        shapes[span.id].char_start, shapes[span.id].char_end = span.char_start, span.char_end
+        touched.add(span.id)
+    for shape_id in touched:
+        shapes[shape_id].reviewer, shapes[shape_id].updated_at = author, now
+
+    gone = set(body.deletes)
+    for shape_id in gone:
+        del shapes[shape_id]
+
+    if body.links is not None:
+        links = list({(link.name, link.from_shape, link.to_shape): link for link in body.links}.values())
+        if dangling := sorted({end for link in links for end in (link.from_shape, link.to_shape)} - shapes.keys()):
+            raise ValidationError(f"link(s) name shape(s) {dangling[:NAMED_IDS]} this task's work does not hold")
+    else:
+        # A deleted shape's links go with it.
+        links = [link for link in links if link.from_shape not in gone and link.to_shape not in gone]
+    return list(shapes.values()), links
+
+
+def _id_type(value: str | int) -> pa.DataType:
+    return pa.string() if isinstance(value, str) else pa.int64()
+
+
+def wire_table(unit: Unit, task_id: str, draft: Draft | None) -> pa.Table:
+    """The draft's shapes as the rows the canvas reads: the unit's identity columns, then `EMPTY_SCHEMA`'s. A row's
+    ``links`` are the links leaving it."""
+    schema = pa.schema([*(pa.field(name, _id_type(value)) for name, value in unit.values.items()), *EMPTY_SCHEMA])
+    shapes = draft.shapes if draft else []
+    outgoing: dict[str, list[dict[str, str]]] = {}
+    for link in draft.links if draft else []:
+        outgoing.setdefault(link.from_shape, []).append({"name": link.name, "to_shape": link.to_shape})
+    rows = [
+        {
+            **unit.values,
+            "id": s.shape_id,
+            "task_id": task_id,
+            "shape_type": s.shape_type,
+            "x": s.x,
+            "y": s.y,
+            "width": s.width,
+            "height": s.height,
+            "rotation": s.rotation,
+            "polygon": s.polygon,
+            "t_start": s.t_start,
+            "t_end": s.t_end,
+            "text": s.text or "",
+            "parent_id": s.parent_id or "",
+            "char_start": -1 if s.char_start is None else s.char_start,
+            "char_end": -1 if s.char_end is None else s.char_end,
+            "label": s.label or "",
+            "status": s.status,
+            "source": s.source or "",
+            "reviewer": s.reviewer,
+            "confidence": s.confidence,
+            "uncertainty": s.uncertainty,
+            "model_version": s.model_version,
+            "group": s.group or "",
+            "difficult": s.difficult,
+            "links": json.dumps(outgoing.get(s.shape_id, []), separators=(",", ":")),
+            "mask": s.mask or "",
+            "metadata": _metadata(s.attributes),
+            "created_at": s.created_at,
+            "updated_at": s.updated_at,
+        }
+        for s in shapes
+    ]
+    return pa.Table.from_pylist(rows, schema=schema)
+
+

+def test_the_history_keeps_the_last_saves_its_byte_bound_holds(work_client: TestClient) -> None:
+    """The history keeps each save's change, not the whole draft, and no more of them than `MAX_HISTORY_BYTES` holds: a
+    task's work costs at most a capped draft and that much history. Saves that each replace a large part of the work push
+    the oldest out, and a read of one pushed out is the 404 of a version the history does not keep."""
+    text = "x" * (MAX_DRAFT_BYTES // 400)
+    rounds = 2 * MAX_HISTORY_BYTES // (MAX_DRAFT_BYTES // 2) + 1
+    for base in range(rounds):
+        _save(
+            work_client,
+            base,
+            inserts=[{"id": f"r{base}-{i}", "shape_type": "tag", "text": text} for i in range(150)],
+            deletes=[f"r{base - 1}-{i}" for i in range(150)] if base else [],
+        )
 
+    kept = [entry["version"] for entry in work_client.get(f"{UNIT}/versions", params={**QUERY, "limit": MAX_DRAFT_HISTORY}).json()]
+    oldest = work_client.get(UNIT, params={**QUERY, "version": kept[-1]})
+    gone = work_client.get(UNIT, params={**QUERY, "version": kept[-1] - 1})
+
+    assert kept == list(range(rounds, kept[-1] - 1, -1)) and 1 < kept[-1] < rounds
+    assert {row["id"] for row in pa.ipc.open_stream(oldest.content).read_all().to_pylist()} == {f"r{kept[-1] - 1}-{i}" for i in range(150)}

+    return sink.getvalue()

-"""ANN-08 — the version history's per-version reads must be cheap and must not run in lockstep.
-
-`GET /api/annotations/{doc}/{speech}/{chunk}/versions` answers one row per Lance version, each row
-carrying the count of THIS unit's annotations at that version. There is no way to answer that
-without touching each version — but there were two ways to make it worse, and both were taken:
-
-* every version was counted by materializing an Arrow table of matching `id`s and reading
-  `.num_rows`, where the count is a pushdown the format already answers;
-* the versions were walked in a `for` loop, so the wall clock was `limit` × (one manifest open +
-  one filtered scan) — up to 200 of them, in series, on S3, holding a threadpool worker.
